options.text: Deacon. I know it's you. I'm not angry. Call me.
Warden. Kitchen door. Now. Or I send your voicemail to the Courier.

script.text: …Don't say it on the phone. Fine. Fine. Yes.
I was nineteen. I washed dishes at the old Waterline. The kitchen window faced the spillway house then too.

18 November 2006. Twenty to midnight. A dark car with council plates, and someone in a long coat in the doorway, and the Voss boy's bicycle against the rail. I took one photo with a cheap camera because I thought it was a couple having an affair.

choice.text: Why the Warden? Why threaten me?

script.text: Then the siren. At night. I'd never heard it at night. And the next week the boy was a runaway and I was a dishwasher who'd seen a car.
I kept the print. Nineteen years in a coffee tin. I've been a coward for exactly as long as I've owned that diner.
Because she came in. Ardis. Eleven days ago, the morning after, and ordered eggs and told me the town looks after its own and looked at my kitchen window the whole time.
I thought if you stopped, she'd have no reason to - I thought Wren would just come back. I'm not a brave man, {player}.

choice.text: Give me the photo. Then we do this together.
Give me the photo. Then stay out of my way.
Give me the photo. And on the day, you come with me to the station.

script.text: …Yes. All right. Together. God help me. It's under the till. Come now, the breakfast crowd's not in yet.
It's under the till. Take it and go. Don't come back to the Waterline after this.
